correctness.rationale: At fixed x and p_n=(log n+x)/n, the original isolates are asymptotically Poisson(lambda=e^-x). For two independently thinned replicas at retention 1-s/log n and 1-t/log n, mixed factorial moments of vertices isolated in both/one-only give independent Poisson mark intensities lambda, lambda(e^s-1), lambda(e^t-1); the common-mark probability tends to the original-isolate probability. The connectivity-without-isolates union bound controls non-isolate disconnections. The joint connectivity limit exp[-lambda(e^s+e^t-1)] gives E(F_n(s)^2) and, after subtracting Z_n*h_x(s), pointwise L2 concentration. Monotonicity and a finite mesh yield uniform compact profile convergence. The annealed isolate variance yields E F_n(s) <= O_x(e^-s+log n/n) uniformly up to s=log n; integrating F_n(s)F_n(t)<=F_n(max{s,t}) controls the squared full tail, proving E|log(n)A(G_n)-C_x Z_n|^2 ->0. This yields a Bernoulli two-atom limit with mean E1(lambda) and variance C_x^2 e^-lambda(1-e^-lambda). Independent rational graph enumeration checked two-retention expectation identities at n=3,4 (27/400, 822771/16000000 for the chosen rational probabilities). Numerical and finite checks are not a proof of the limit.

value.rationale: The probability that a critical random network is connected stays bounded between zero and one, so fixed-network reliability has a natural persistent random component. Establishing a quenched L2 profile and non-self-averaging two-atom area limit resolves a genuinely probabilistic refinement of average all-terminal reliability, beyond its easy annealed connectivity integral. The precise limiting conditional constant and variance are natural network-reliability statistics.

limitations: No uniform rate in x; only the fixed connectivity window and asymptotic L2 law.
